rows: Wait-Process waits for specified process IDs; Microsoft distinguishes it from Start-Process -Wait, which waits for the process tree.
A direct-PID timeout does not by itself prove descendant cleanup.
Start-Process launches a local process and supports waiting for the process and descendants.
Executable and argument identity still require application-level pinning.
Stop-Process targets processes by ID or name and may require elevated rights.
Stopping one PID does not establish process-tree cleanup.
Get-CimInstance can query Win32_Process process metadata.
Broad command-line substring matching is not an exact process identity contract.
Win32_Process exposes process identifiers, parent identifiers, executable paths, command lines and creation data.
Consumers must explicitly validate the fields they rely on.
ConvertTo-Json serializes PowerShell objects with configurable depth.
Serialization alone does not make publication atomic or schema-valid.
Set-Content replaces file content at a target path.
Direct final-path writes can expose partial or replayable receipts.
Get-FileHash computes file hashes including SHA-256.
A hash observed before execution does not close a later path TOCTOU window.
git fetch supports atomic reference updates and explicit remote/ref selection.
Repository origin identity and exact fetched head remain separate checks.
Fast-forward policy does not validate executable identity or receipt freshness.
git stash push --include-untracked includes untracked files in the stash operation.
A later refs/stash existence check does not prove which stash was created.
git rev-parse resolves revisions and repository information.
Resolved names must be bound to the intended repository and invocation.
git hash-object computes Git object IDs from file bytes.
Path content may change after hashing unless execution is immutably bound.
git merge-base --is-ancestor can test fast-forward ancestry.
Ancestry checks do not authenticate the remote repository.
git status --porcelain provides script-oriented worktree state.
A status snapshot should be durably preserved before mutations.
Git configuration controls remotes, hooks, credentials and process behavior.
Recovery needs an explicit trusted configuration and origin policy.
Subprocess timeouts raise TimeoutExpired; process and pipe handling require explicit management.
Timeout of a direct child is not a universal descendant-cleanup receipt.
Python JSON defaults allow non-standard NaN unless strict options are used.
Receipts need strict parsing, duplicate-key policy and schema validation.
Resolved paths and replace operations support containment and atomic-pointer designs.
Symlink, reparse and durability policy must still be enforced.
The current INSPIRE dataset publication is 5 July 2026.
Catalogue publication does not prove current downloaded archive bytes.
HMLR documents GML and British National Grid processing context.
Fresh native file, identity and geometry receipts remain required.
The official DTM 1m dataset identifies the primary elevation product and EPSG:27700 context.
Metadata does not establish fresh WCS response bytes.
Terrain 50 grid supply uses 200 by 200 cells, 50 metre spacing and 10 km tiles.
Exact package, edition and sidecar hashes remain required.
WCS separates capabilities, coverage description and coverage retrieval.
Service, domain, range and response identity must remain bound.
